meta.note: Real data, aggregated from a personal end-of-day tracking log (2026-08-29 through 2026-09-25). Customer/account names anonymized. Only entries with a directly comparable AI-assisted vs. estimated-unassisted time are counted in the hours/multiplier stats below — entries marked 'not previously possible' or 'pending' are tracked separately rather than forced into a ratio. Unassisted estimates use the low end of any range.

scopeExpansion.title: Autonomous case tracking
scopeExpansion.before: Reviewing and escalating cases was a multi-day manual cycle per pass.
scopeExpansion.after: A fully autonomous tracker pulls, reviews, and alerts on cases daily — runs in minutes, no manual cycle required.

scopeExpansion.title: Data that was effectively unreachable
scopeExpansion.before: Key account identifiers were scattered across disconnected system fields, not reliably visible at all.
scopeExpansion.after: Sourced and reconciled in about an hour — not realistically doable manually in the time available.

scopeExpansion.title: This journal itself
scopeExpansion.before: No system existed for tracking personal output — it just didn't happen.
scopeExpansion.after: Designed and running within a day and a half, entirely in conversation, with no separate tool to learn.

scopeExpansion.title: Rush turnarounds
scopeExpansion.before: Consolidating account data into revenue-tied materials alone, under time pressure, wasn't realistic for one person.
scopeExpansion.after: Pulled, consolidated, and turned into finished slides in an afternoon.

scopeExpansion.title: Business-review prep that schedules itself
scopeExpansion.before: Spotting upcoming customer reviews meant checking a tracker by hand and remembering to block prep time.
scopeExpansion.after: A scheduler reads the review tracker, and anything inside a 30-day window gets a reminder task and, when the timing is known, a prep block on the calendar.

scopeExpansion.title: A weekly recap nobody had time to write
scopeExpansion.before: No weekly summary existed. Open loops and action items lived in scattered meetings, threads, and notes.
scopeExpansion.after: A recap pulls the week's meetings, email, chat, and notes into a manager-ready summary, and flags mismatched notes instead of guessing.

scopeExpansion.title: Building for other teams
scopeExpansion.before: Other teams' tracking gaps weren't mine to solve, and there was no time to try.
scopeExpansion.after: Built a support-case tracker for another team and a log-run automation for a colleague, about two hours each.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: Walk me through today — what did you actually produce?

sampleInterview.speaker: user
sampleInterview.text: I got the manual trigger working for a reporting run that used to be fully manual — now it's just a 15-minute trigger.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: Got it, that's Automation / AI Tooling. Before this, how long did that reporting take start to finish?

sampleInterview.speaker: user
sampleInterview.text: Probably an hour, sometimes two, depending on how messy the source data was.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: Logged: 15 minutes assisted vs. roughly an hour-plus estimated. Anything else today?

sampleInterview.speaker: user
sampleInterview.text: Yeah, I also sourced some account identifiers that were scattered across a few disconnected system fields.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: That's data wrangling. Realistically, could you have pulled that together manually in the time you had?

sampleInterview.speaker: user
sampleInterview.text: Honestly, no — not without hours I didn't have.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: Logging that one as 'not previously possible' rather than a time comparison — that's its own category, and it matters as much as the hours saved.

roadmap.title: Manual end-of-day interview
roadmap.detail: Conversational capture, no live logging. Entries categorized and estimated together at day's end, running on real data since late August 2026.

roadmap.title: Calendar-aware capture
roadmap.detail: Entries are now drafted from the day's calendar blocks and reviewed and corrected, instead of retold from scratch. A weekly-recap tool reads calendar, email, chat, and meeting notes; a week-ahead planner is built and awaiting its first full run.

roadmap.title: AI-populated tasks
roadmap.detail: A first version is live: upcoming business reviews automatically become reminder tasks and calendar prep blocks. Next step is duplicate protection so it can run on a schedule.

roadmap.title: A template for the team
roadmap.detail: Package the pattern so colleagues outside engineering can run their own journal and dashboard, giving a bigger sample than one person's data.
